newsitem.title: INDIA: India decision on sugar prices after state polls.
newsitem.headline: India decision on sugar prices after state polls.

text.p: The Indian cabinet on Monday did not take up a proposed hike in issue prices for levy sugar which is now expected to be taken up after the assembly elections in the northern state of Punjab, a government spokesman said.
"The election process is on. They (cabinet) have decided to take a view on this later,"the spokesman said.
Election in Punjab are scheduled to take place on February 7.
The cabinet was expected to consider Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra's proposal to raise issue prices by 1.60 rupees per kg. The current issue price is 9.05 rupees per kg.
The issue price is the rate at which the government sells sugar to the public distribution system.
Earlier this month, Indian new agencies quoted Mishra as saying that federal subsidies would rise by 7.2 billion rupees if state-controlled sugar prices were not increased by 1.60 rupees per kg.
Sugar supplies and pricing in India are controlled by the government.
Millers supply 40 percent of their output to the government at below-market rates for distribution through government shops at subsidised prices.
